What Is a Good Half Marathon Time for Beginners?

A good half marathon time for a beginner is one that reflects your own fitness, and for most first-timers that means finishing somewhere around two to three hours. To put your goal in context, this page gives the average finish times for recreational runners, the pace you'd need for common goal times, and a simple way to predict your own time from a recent 5K or 10K.

Average half marathon times

RunRepeat's "State of Running 2019" analysed 107.9 million race results from more than 70,000 events between 1986 and 2018, with elite runners excluded. It reports average half marathon paces of 5:40 per km for men and 6:22 per km for women. Over the full distance, those paces work out to roughly:

  • Men: about 1:59:30 (9:07 per mile)
  • Women: about 2:14:20 (10:15 per mile)

These averages include experienced recreational runners, not just first-timers, so many beginners will finish slower. That's completely normal. The source doesn't give half marathon averages by age, so we don't either.

Predict your time from a 5K or 10K

Peter Riegel's race-time formula is the standard way to estimate a longer race from a shorter one. For the half marathon it works out to roughly:

  • From a 10K: your 10K time × 2.2. For example, a 60-minute 10K predicts about 2:12, and a 50-minute 10K about 1:50.
  • From a 5K: your 5K time × 4.6. For example, a 30-minute 5K predicts about 2:18.

The prediction assumes you've done half-marathon training, especially long runs. Don't add an extra margin on top, because the multiplier already allows for the longer distance. If you haven't trained the distance yet, treat the result as a target to train toward, not a pace to start the race at.

Pacing your first half marathon

  • Run the first few kilometres slightly slower than goal pace. It's the easiest way to avoid fading late in the race.
  • Settle into goal pace through the middle miles.
  • Pick it up over the last 5K only if you feel strong.

In training, keep easy runs conversational: about 60–90 seconds per mile (35–55 seconds per km) slower than your goal race pace. That's the same guidance as our marathon plans.

How long to train

If you can already run about 3 miles (5 km) without stopping, 12 weeks is enough for most beginners. Our 12-week half marathon training plan has every week in miles and kilometres. Strength training twice a week is worth adding: a 2018 systematic review in Sports Medicine found that strength training generally improved running economy by 2–8% compared with running alone.

FAQ

Is 2:30 a good first half marathon time?

Yes. It means averaging about 7:07 per km (11:27 per mile) for 21.1 km, which is a solid result for a first race.

Is a sub-2 hour half marathon realistic for a beginner?

It requires about 5:41 per km (9:09 per mile). A 10K of about 54–55 minutes predicts a time close to two hours. If your recent 10K is much slower than that, set a nearer goal for your first race.

How much faster will my second half marathon be?

That depends on your training. Most runners improve with more consistent mileage and better pacing, so use your first result to set the next goal.
